newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak c.bank to offer last-resort help to budget.
newsitem.headline: Slovak c.bank to offer last-resort help to budget.

text.p: The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) said on Thursday it would participate in the financing of the state budget only as the lender of last resort.

"We intend to avoid as far as possible being the factor of the state budget financing, but for the time being it is acceptable for us due to the current market illiquidity," Juraj Janosik, a head of the NBS Banking Transactions Department, told Reuters.
Earlier on Thursday, the NBS took a 1.0 billion crown tranche of the finance ministry's seven-day treasury bills into its own portfolio. It was the first T-bill tranche the NBS bought this year.
Janosik said the NBS the central bank's participation on the current budget financing has been "relatively low" so far, but its effort is to keep it at an "emergency" level.
"The problem (of the budget financing) is still open," Janosik added.
Slovakia's overall 1997 state budget deficit is planned at 36.9 billion crowns, compared with the deficit of 27 billion crowns last year.
The government plans issuing 70 billion crowns worth of its securities on domestic markets this year.

In its Wednesday's auction of four-week T-bills, the ministry accepted all bids worth mere 959 million crowns, at an average yield of 13.64 percent after 12.55 percent in the last auction of similar bills on December 30.
